summary: Fix X2 in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/pmdoc. (1) position.go len16: range over the string, +1 unit per rune and +1 more above U+FFFF (as api/server.go:803), allocation-free and exactly equal to len(utf16.Encode([]rune(s))). (2) walk.go: walk fills one pre-order []int of subtree sizes bottom-up, following walkNode's descent rule (text, leaf, nil, doc, other), with the size rule written once and shared with nodeSize; walkNode reads sizes by pre-order index; visit order, path, early stop and nil handling unchanged; no pool, no cache on Node; walk's doc comment says visitors must not change Text/Children of unvisited nodes. (3) splice.go insertAt visitor returns at once for pos outside [start,end] (exact), so childBoundary runs only on ancestors of pos. Then tests, corpus equivalence, micro-benchmark, merge rule on INFRA-639's replay, suites, changelog.
tasks: 1. len16 in position.go; position_test.go: TestLen16CountsTheUnitsUTF16EncodingWrites (edge table incl. invalid bytes, ED A0 80, F4 90 80 80, truncated sequences, NUL, U+FFFF, U+10000, U+10FFFF) vs reference len(utf16.Encode([]rune(s))); FuzzLen16 seeded with the table; AllocsPerRun == 0.

2. Sized walk in walk.go; new walk_test.go with a frozen reference copy of today's walkNode/nodeSize/len16; TestWalkVisitsEveryNodeWithTodaysRange over testdata/corpus/*.md, fixtures.json, synthetic edge trees (astral, empty texts, mark-split text, every leaf type, text/leaf with children, nil child, non-doc root, MaxTreeDepth chain, wide doc) and a generated >=400 KB depth>=10 doc; early stop at several k; Size equal; failure messages never print text; BenchmarkPositionedWalk (real-size, depth 5 vs 20 same node count) with ReportAllocs.

3. insertAt early return in splice.go:180-192; existing insert/edit tests lock it; throwaway comparison at every position of every corpus doc against a test-local copy of today's visitor, then removed.

4. Opt-in TestWalkMatchesTodaysWalkOnACorpus (PMDOC_WALK_CORPUS dir of .md): Parse, Update into Y fragment, proofComment marks on every 50th text node, Read; visits, len16 per text node and Size equal to the reference on both trees; logs counts only. Corpus: every LINUX spec fetched read-only under $TMPDIR/x2-corpus with dispatch issues/doc-read; never committed. Negative control: break len16 or the +2 once, record the first-mismatch line, restore.

5. Micro-benchmark base vs head from a git archive export: go test -run '^$' -bench BenchmarkPositionedWalk -benchmem -count 8; benchstat golang.org/x/perf/cmd/benchstat@v0.0.0-20261009192801-be2c69fb417e.

6. Merge rule on LINUX's replay from C (main if INFRA-639's replay merged, else legion/INFRA-639 at the commit its implementer reports working): git archive C as base, C + this PR's diff as head; seed once with base; six interleaved run-step.sh runs; box_busy_before < 10%, no exited process; figure = Dispatch CPU-s over the replay (per committed write if commits differ); pass when every head run < every base run, else the profile-share route (len16 + nodeSize + sizing function cum, plus walkNode flat) by at least half the expected gain (~61% of base CPU without X1 in C, ~10% with it); alloc_space reported; PR names C and the diff fingerprint.
7. gofmt, go vet, go test pmdoc (and -race), docs and api with DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL on a local pgserver Postgres (no docker in the pod).
8. packages/envoy/CHANGELOG.md Unreleased / Changed entry with measured numbers.
9. ce-simplify-code once, PR body per legion-worker pr-body.md with 'Dispatch: INFRA-641'.

findings.finding: The merge rule's input (INFRA-639's LINUX replay) does not exist yet and the load test (PR #2369) is not on main.
findings.answer: Task 6 measures from the commit C that carries the replay (main or legion/INFRA-639), as the spec's fallback says; tasks 1-5 and 7-9 proceed; the implementer waits for INFRA-639 and tells the architect rather than measuring with throwaway tools or merging without it (those would be the architect's call).

findings.finding: Expected gains are modelled production cores, the base (with or without X1) is not chosen, and the changed function's share is undefined.
findings.answer: Task 6 converts the gain to the load test's units for each base (about 61% of base CPU without X1, about 10% with it, from ranking section 4.1), names the profile share (len16, nodeSize and the sizing function cum, plus walkNode flat) and its pprof command, and the base is whatever C is at measurement, named in the PR.

findings.finding: Which CPU figure decides, and the load test's Postgres (16.2 pgserver) differs from the spec's Postgres 17 debs.
findings.answer: The figure is Dispatch CPU-seconds over the replay as INFRA-639 reports it, per committed write when commits differ; the Postgres is the load test's, the same for both sides, recorded (departure 2).

findings.finding: The 77% allocation figure is from the bench, and the sizes slice adds bytes; a sync.Pool may count as resident memory.
findings.answer: Allocation is reported (alloc_space medians) beside the merge rule, not a separate gate, and 77% is quoted only when C lacks X1; no pool and no cache on Node; benchmark quotes B/op and allocs/op; one []int of 8 bytes per visited node per walk.

findings.finding: Once the change lands there is nothing to compare against; the visitor contract includes order, path and early stop.
findings.answer: walk_test.go keeps a frozen reference copy of today's walkNode/nodeSize/len16 and compares every visit's (node pointer, path, pos, end), early stops at several k, and Size.

findings.finding: The 1,157-spec proof needs an opt-in test, a stated tree source, no spec text in public logs, and committed synthetic edge cases.
findings.answer: Task 4: PMDOC_WALK_CORPUS opt-in test, trees both parsed and read back from a Y fragment with proofComment marks; logs counts only; task 2 commits synthetic astral, empty-text, leaf, nil-child, non-doc-root, nested cases.

findings.finding: len16 feeds CRDT offsets and needs machine-checkable equality incl. invalid bytes, encoded surrogates, above-U+10FFFF and truncated sequences; utf16.RuneLen returns -1 for surrogates.
findings.answer: Task 1: edge-case table and FuzzLen16 against the reference, AllocsPerRun == 0; RuneLen not used.

findings.finding: childBoundary keeps insertAt at nodes x depth; in scope or not?
findings.answer: In scope (departure 1): an exact early return in insertAt's visitor for pos outside [start,end]; existing tests plus a throwaway all-positions comparison on the corpus.

findings.finding: The pre-order index must follow walkNode's descent rule exactly (text/leaf with children, nil child, non-doc root).
findings.answer: Design 2 shares one size rule between nodeSize and the sizing pass; task 2's synthetic cases include each of these.

findings.finding: Precomputed sizes add a rule that visitors must not change sizes during the walk.
findings.answer: Design 4 adds that sentence to walk's doc comment; no positioned-walk visitor writes Text or Children today.

findings.finding: Fit with siblings X1 (INFRA-640) and INFRA-649: re-measuring if X1 merges in between, anything exposed.
findings.answer: Nothing is exported; the measurement names its base; main is taken in only on a real conflict, and a conflict in walk.go, position.go or splice.go repeats task 6.
Task 8 adds one under Unreleased / Changed in packages/envoy/CHANGELOG.md.

findings.finding: The spec's '48% of all bytes' has no source; the replay report says 47% (104 of 222 GB).
findings.answer: Noted; the plan and PR quote 47% from the replay report and the measured figures of this change.

specDepartures.spec: Count UTF-16 units without allocating and compute subtree sizes once per walk (pmdoc/position.go len16, pmdoc/walk.go walkNode/nodeSize).
specDepartures.plan: Also makes insertAt's walk visitor (pmdoc/splice.go:180-192) return at once for nodes whose range [start,end] cannot hold the insertion position, so childBoundary no longer sums nodeSize over every visited node's children.
specDepartures.evidence: splice.go:185 calls childBoundary for every visited node and splice.go:234-249 sums nodeSize over its children: O(nodes x depth) on every doc-edit insert. childBoundary can only match inside [start+1,end-1] for a non-doc node and [0,end] for doc, and the inline condition lies inside it too, so the return is exact.

outcome.scope: Adds pmdoc/splice.go's insertAt visitor to the change; acceptance and settled decisions unchanged.

specDepartures.spec: The Dispatch server run locally against Postgres 17 with pgvector (from unpacked .debs).
specDepartures.plan: Uses the Postgres the load test itself installs (pgserver wheel: Postgres 16.2 with pgvector), the same for base and head runs, recorded from meta.json.
specDepartures.evidence: INFRA-589's load test README (Requirements and 'The database'): stack.sh setup installs Postgres 16.2 and pgvector from the pgserver wheel; the spec also says the change is driven by that one load test.
